problem.name: Deutsch–Jozsa promise problem
problem.statement_latex: Given oracle access to $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, promised to be constant or balanced, decide which case holds. The exact and bounded-error query models give different comparisons.
problem.statement_text: Given oracle access to $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, promised to be constant or balanced, decide which case holds. The exact and bounded-error query models give different comparisons.

strength.description_latex: Exponential to polynomial for exact worst-case decision; constant-error randomized testing has constant query complexity.
strength.description_text: Exponential to polynomial for exact worst-case decision; constant-error randomized testing has constant query complexity.

evidence.description_latex: The cited results establish a classical lower bound separating the stated quantum resource bound in the specified model.
evidence.description_text: The cited results establish a classical lower bound separating the stated quantum resource bound in the specified model.

hardware.description_latex: The transform circuit uses $O(n)$ logical qubits and $O(n)$ elementary gates around its oracle calls; implementing the oracle determines the full device cost. Small circuit demonstrations are feasible.
hardware.description_text: The transform circuit uses $O(n)$ logical qubits and $O(n)$ elementary gates around its oracle calls; implementing the oracle determines the full device cost. Small circuit demonstrations are feasible.

quantum.headline_latex: One exact oracle query and $O(n)$ additional gates by the Deutsch--Jozsa Hadamard-transform circuit.
quantum.headline_text: One exact oracle query and $O(n)$ additional gates by the Deutsch–Jozsa Hadamard-transform circuit.

classical.headline_latex: $2^{n-1}+1$ worst-case queries for exact classical decision; bounded-error randomized testing uses $O(1)$ samples at constant confidence.
classical.headline_text: $2^{n-1}+1$ worst-case queries for exact classical decision; bounded-error randomized testing uses $O(1)$ samples at constant confidence.
